name: High Priestess Nerissa
description: High Priestess of the Temple of the Lake Lady -- middle-aged, silver-streaked hair, blue-green robes that ripple like water. A powerful divine caster (Piety 92, Willpower 85) who senses water corruption, blesses sacred waters, and speaks with water spirits. Temple law forbids her from intervening directly, so she works through the PCs.
narrative: Nerissa is High Priestess at the Temple of the Lake Lady, a serene, formidable woman with silver-streaked dark hair and blue-green robes that seem to ripple like water as she moves. She senses corruption within sacred waters, performs water-based blessing rituals, and communicates with the Lake Lady's water spirits. Since the Baron's arrival she has been tracking a steady rise in that corruption -- but temple law forbids her from intervening directly unless the sacred sites themselves are threatened. So she becomes a patron: supplying spiritual support, ritual knowledge, and the water-magic countermeasures the players will need, while relying on them to act where she cannot.

extras.role: High Priestess at the Temple of the Lake Lady. Middle-aged, silver-streaked dark hair, blue-green robes that ripple like water when she moves.
extras.constraint: Bound by temple law: cannot directly intervene unless sacred sites are threatened -- she needs the PCs as agents. Provides spiritual support, ritual knowledge, and water-magic countermeasures. Tracking rising corruption since the Baron's arrival.
extras.magic_tradition: Theism / divine (Classic Fantasy Cleric) at the top of her order -- Devotion (Piety) 92, Exhort 80, Lore (Theology, Lake Lady) 88. A genuinely high-level cleric: she can Heal, Raise Dead, Part Water, Commune, Quest, Atone, and True See. Her power is in healing, water, ward, judgement and asking her goddess questions. She has NO possession magic of any kind -- no Exorcise, no Spirit Sight -- and the Order never has had. Her water-sensitivity is a power, not a spell: she feels what has gone INTO the water and it has never told her what is standing next to her.
extras.spell_access: CFI cleric, Rank 4: access to every cleric spell of that Rank or below. "memorized" is what is currently prayed for, not what she can have.
extras.magic: The rites, her sensing of the Lady's waters, and the doctrine that the Order has never had possession magic are all one power: magic/powers/the-rites-of-the-lady. Read it before playing her doing anything magical.

actor_notes:
High Priestess Nerissa
LOOKS: Fifties. Blue-green worked so heavily with silver that the light does something strange on the cloth.
CORE: A woman who has been right, alone, for two years, about something enormous, and who has been kindly and patiently managed by every person she told. She is not bitter about it. She is worse than bitter: she has become careful.
NATURE: Grave, dry, and physically fearless -- she drinks the fouled water herself and has told nobody why. Not warm in manner but unusually kind in practice; when somebody is in trouble in front of her she simply deals with it, without commentary.
WOUND: She can feel what is happening to the water in her own body, and the Order's answer was to have a younger priestess sit with her. She has been managing her own credibility ever since like a woman managing a small fire.
WANTS: Somebody with standing to say out loud the thing she is not permitted to say.
PRESSURE: She stops being careful. The hedging drops off and she starts stating things flatly and in public, and everyone around her who knows her goes very quiet, because this is the thing they have all been afraid of.
KEY: "I am permitted to be wrong about this. That is the whole of what I am permitted."
MAGIC: Formidable at home and an ordinary middle-aged woman on a dredge-boat -- her weight is the rites, and the rites need the temple, the pool, the Order and time. She has no possession magic of any kind and the Order never has had; that province belongs to the demonologists and the wild-elf druids.

powers.name: The Rites of the Lady
limits: Limited Power -- the place, the people and the time, or it does not happen
